body.statement: For any fixed nonempty finite \(\mathfrak G\), nonempty compact boxes, exponent array, and nonempty open \(\mathcal O\subset(0,1)^p\), there are a finite rational \(\mathcal T\subset\mathcal O\), a rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\), and a valid finite rational chart-projection cover \(\mathscr C\) such that \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0\), \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\), and \(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\). Here \(\Gamma_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when \(|\mathfrak G|=1\), and \(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}=+\infty\) when its remote pair set is empty. Consequently each within-graph moment map is globally injective; this uses local chart strong monotonicity and remote separation, not the Jacobian margin alone.
body.justification: This establishes existence of a finite transform design with distinct global and local certificates.
body.gap: Bodik--Chavez-Demoulin supplies neither a finite PGF grid nor quantitative global-injectivity and Jacobian margins over compact boxes.
body.consumer: It supplies the consistency check that the reusable certificate is searching for a nonvacuous finite-input object.
body.proof_tex:
Apply the polynomial-PGF regularity lemma to each of the finitely many graph tuples.  Write \(F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)\) for the stacked type PGFs at a single point \(z\in\mathcal O\).  If \(v\) is a unit parameter direction, injectivity of the distributional differential and signed-PGF uniqueness imply that
\[
D_\theta F_{\boldsymbol d}(\theta,z)v\ne0
\quad\text{for some }z\in\mathcal O. \tag{20}
\]
For fixed \(\boldsymbol d\), the product of \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) and its parameter unit sphere is compact.  Continuity makes the nonvanishing in (20) persist on a neighborhood of \((\theta,v)\).  A finite subcover supplies finitely many points \(z\) such that their stacked Jacobian has trivial kernel for every \(\theta\).  Its smallest singular value is continuous, so its minimum on \(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\) is positive.

Uniform continuity of this finite stacked Jacobian gives a number \(r_0>0\) for which the integral Taylor formula separates every within-graph pair at distance less than \(r_0\).  Fix a positive rational \(r_1<r_0\).  Within a graph, two distinct parameters induce different laws.  If their PGFs agreed on the nonempty open set \(\mathcal O\), successive one-variable power-series uniqueness would make their laws equal, a contradiction.  On the compact set
\[
\{(\theta,\theta')\in\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}^2:
\|\theta-\theta'\|_2\geq r_1\}, \tag{21}
\]
each pair is consequently separated by some PGF evaluation.  A finite subcover of (21) supplies finitely many separating points.  The same argument applies to each compact product
\(\Theta_{\boldsymbol d}\times\Theta_{\boldsymbol d'}\) for
\(\boldsymbol d\ne\boldsymbol d'\), because the regularity lemma gives disjoint law images.

Take the union of all points selected in the preceding two paragraphs.  There are only finitely many graph tuples and graph pairs.  All the asserted full-rank and separation properties are strict and uniform on compact sets.  Joint continuity in the evaluation points permits each selected point to be perturbed to a rational point still in the open set \(\mathcal O\), without losing any property.  Denote the resulting finite rational grid by \(\mathcal T\).  It gives
\[
\kappa_{\mathcal T}>0,\qquad
\Gamma_{\mathcal T}>0
\]
when a wrong graph exists; the declared \(+\infty\) convention handles a singleton graph class.

We next construct the local charts, because Jacobian rank alone does not prove global injectivity.  At every \(\theta\), full column rank of
\(J_{\boldsymbol d,\mathcal T}(\theta)\) gives a real left inverse
\[
L_\theta=(J^{\mathsf T}J)^{-1}J^{\mathsf T},
\qquad L_\theta J=I.
\]
Approximate \(L_\theta\) closely enough by a rational matrix \(P_\theta\).  Continuity of \(J\) then supplies a relative neighborhood \(U_\theta\) in the box on which
\[
\frac{P_\theta J(\vartheta)+
J(\vartheta)^{\mathsf T}P_\theta^{\mathsf T}}2
\succeq c_\theta I,\qquad c_\theta>0. \tag{22}
\]
Compactness and the rational rectangular shape of the parameter box give a finite cover by closed rational sub-boxes \(C_{\boldsymbol d c}\), each lying in one such neighborhood and carrying its corresponding rational \(P_{\boldsymbol d c}\), whose relative interiors still cover the parameter box.  A Lebesgue number of this finite relative open cover is positive.  Choose rational \(r_{\mathrm{id}}>0\) smaller than that number and smaller than \(r_1\).  Then every pair less than \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) apart is co-contained in a chart.

For \(\theta,\theta'\) in one convex chart, put \(\Delta=\theta'-\theta\).  The fundamental theorem of calculus and (22) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\langle P_{\boldsymbol d c}\{m(\theta')-m(\theta)\},\Delta\rangle
&=\int_0^1
\Delta^{\mathsf T}P_{\boldsymbol d c}
J(\theta+t\Delta)\Delta\,dt\\
&=\int_0^1
\Delta^{\mathsf T}\frac{PJ+J^{\mathsf T}P^{\mathsf T}}2
\Delta\,dt\\
&\geq c_{\boldsymbol d c}\|\Delta\|_2^2 .
\end{aligned} \tag{23}
\]
The finite minimum of the positive chart constants proves
\(\mu_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}};\mathscr C)>0\).

Finally, the remote set with distance at least \(r_{\mathrm{id}}\) is compact.  Pairs at distance at least \(r_1\) are separated by the finite-cover points selected from (21), while pairs at distance in \([r_{\mathrm{id}},r_1]\) are separated by the local Taylor bound from the uniformly nonsingular stacked Jacobian.  Hence the already selected finite grid separates the whole remote set, so its continuous squared \(W\)-distance has a positive minimum, namely
\(\Lambda_{\mathcal T}(r_{\mathrm{id}})>0\); if the set is empty the declared value is \(+\infty\).  A local pair is separated by (23), and a remote pair by this last bound.  Thus every within-graph moment map is globally injective, with the four distinct margins claimed.
